cards.front: Recall a key point about The Role of Education
cards.back: Functionalist view: education serves vital functions for society. Durkheim: education transmits society's norms and values (social solidarity) and teaches specialist skills for the division of labour. Parsons: education is the main agent of secondary socialisation and a bridge between family and wider society; it promotes meritocracy (everyone has equal opportunity to succeed based on ability and effort).

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Role of Education
cards.back: Marxist view: education serves capitalism. Althusser: education is an Ideological State Apparatus (ISA) that transmits ruling class ideology, making inequality seem natural and inevitable. Bowles and Gintis: the correspondence principle - schools mirror the workplace through the hidden curriculum (hierarchy, competition, obedience to authority, punctuality) preparing workers for capitalist exploitation.

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Role of Education
cards.back: Feminist view: education is patriarchal. Historically: girls were steered towards domestic subjects and away from science/maths. Kelly: the curriculum is male-dominated (textbooks feature men, examples from male experiences). Modern challenge: despite girls outperforming boys, women still face a glass ceiling in careers and are underrepresented in STEM subjects.

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Role of Education
cards.back: The hidden curriculum: the unwritten, unofficial lessons that schools teach - obedience to authority, competition, conformity, acceptance of hierarchy, punctuality. Functionalists see this as positive (teaches social norms); Marxists see it as negative (prepares workers for exploitation).

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Role of Education
cards.back: Vocational education and training: provides work-based skills. Functionalists argue it meets the economy's need for skilled workers. Marxists argue it creates a compliant, low-paid workforce and reproduces class inequality (working-class students are steered towards vocational courses, middle-class towards academic).

cards.front: What should you know about sociology exam tips?
cards.back: When evaluating the role of education, always compare perspectives, use named sociologists and concepts, and provide evidence for whether education serves all groups equally or reproduces inequality.

Students often make mistakes here. Wrong: The education system gives everyone an equal chance to succeed regardless of their background. Evaluate the view that the education system serves the interests of the ruling class.

cards.back: AO1 — Knowledge: Show knowledge of The Role of Education using sociological terminology accurately. Identify key thinkers, concepts and theoretical perspectives.
